subject: Dedicated reservation economics & throughput — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@horizonhealth.ai>, Horizon Health Procurement <procurement@horizonhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation economics & throughput — post-demo next steps

Hi Emily / team,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the candid traffic patterns you shared. Per our call, below is a concise recap and a set of asks so we can produce a firm reserved-capacity proposal: 

Recap of what I heard:
- Workload: real-time patient triage + summarization flows. Average generation ~400 tokens, model family: tuned Llama-derivative (70B-ish).
- Current baseline: ~95M tokens/day average (≈1,100 tokens/s sustained).
- Peaks: up to ~60 RPS with bursts lasting minutes (60 RPS * 400 tokens ≈ 24,000 tokens/s peak).
- Target latency SLO: 75–150ms p50/p95 for single-turn generation.
- Initial procurement timeline: decision target within 3 weeks; POC requested.

Preliminary economics asks (we need these confirmed):
1) Target unit cost you want us to hit (your stated goal on the call): $/1M tokens target range.
2) Budget range for a reserved capacity commitment (monthly).
3) Preferred GPU family (if you have an ops preference): H100 vs A100 (we can recommend).
4) Desired reservation size floor (number of GPUs) — if you have a minimum commitment in mind.

What we'll produce once we have the confirms:
- 2 capacity options (sustained vs. burst headroom) with mapped throughput, expected p50/p95, and an estimated $/1M-token blended rate.
- A 30-day POC proposal (technical runbook + acceptance criteria).
- Contract sketch for reserved capacity (term/commit/early exit).

I attached a short pricing playbook + a rough estimate spreadsheet to help guide your procurement discussion.

Next suggested steps:
- Emily: confirm the three items above (unit-cost target, budget band, GPU preference) by EOD Mon 6/15 if possible.
- We will turn around a tailored 2-option proposal by Wed 6/17 for your procurement review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if you want to walk the numbers together.

Best,
Avery Johnson

avery.johnson@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@horizonhealth.ai>

Cc: Horizon Health Procurement <procurement@horizonhealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation economics & throughput — post-demo next steps

Hi Avery — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the items from our side so you can firm up the proposal: 

1) Unit-cost target: we're aiming for ~$10 per 1M tokens as a conversation target. We'd be willing to stretch to $12/1M if latency and availability guarantees are strong and if we can get reasonable burst capacity.
2) Budget band: procurement is targeting an initial committed monthly spend of $20k–$35k (we understand commits map to reserved GPU counts).
3) GPU preference: ops has a soft preference for H100 (we run other workloads on H100 and prefer consistency), but procurement is open to A100 if the price delta is meaningful.
4) Reservation size: no hard minimum from a product POV, but procurement is thinking in terms of a 4–12 GPU reserved window for the initial term.

Traffic clarifications: average tokens/day ~95M (as you put). For bursts — our observed busiest windows are 08:00–11:00 PT where latency must be tight; recent test bursts show peaks of ~60 RPS with average response ~400 tokens. We can provide a sample 24h traffic CSV if that helps.

POC: yes to the 30-day POC with acceptance criteria focused on p95 latency under burst and an estimate of sustained $/1M tokens post-optimizations (batching/quant).

Next step: please propose Option A/B with mapped GPU counts and an expected blended $/1M token estimate by Wed 6/17. Procurement will review and follow up on commercial terms.

—Emily
Emily Sanders
Director, Digital Experience | Horizon Health
emily.sanders@horizonhealth.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated reservation economics & throughput — internal SE notes

Avery / Neha — quick SE sketch for the two options we should hand back to Emily. Numbers are rough but designed to map to their $/1M target and burst profile.

Assumptions:
- Model: Llama-derivative 70B (int8 / q4 optimization available).
- Average response: 400 tokens. Peak: 60 RPS (burst). Sustained average: 1,100 tokens/s.
- H100 baseline throughput (generation, approx): 3,500–6,000 tokens/s per GPU depending on batch/quant. H100 has better perf for fp16 + q4.
- A100 baseline throughput (generation, approx): 2,000–3,500 tokens/s per GPU.

Option A — Cost-optimized (preferred if they want to hit ~$10/1M):
- Reserved: 6 x H100 (reserved pool), config: autoscale burst to +2 spare when needed (burst policy).
- Expected sustained throughput headroom: ~20–30k tokens/s (enough to cover 24k spikes with queuing/batching).
- Estimated blended $/1M tokens: $8–$11 (post-batching & quantization savings).
- Pros: price hit for them, meets their budget band if priced ~ $22k–$30k/mo.
- Cons: tighter ops margin on very large burst windows; will require careful caching and prefix-KV tuning.

Option B — Latency/availability-optimized:
- Reserved: 10 x H100 (more headroom).
- Expected sustained throughput headroom: ~35–50k tokens/s; much lower p95 under peak.
- Estimated blended $/1M tokens: $11–$16.
- Pros: lower p95, safer for 08:00–11:00 windows.
- Cons: cost above their sweet spot; procurement may push back.

POC proposal (30d):
- Provide Option A config in a POC with telemetry: per-token cost dashboard, p50/p95 latency under a synthetic 60 RPS burst, and an optimization pass (int8/q4) to verify the $/1M estimate.
- Acceptance: p95 < 250ms during defined 10-minute synthetic peak and a verified blended cost within 20% of the proposal.

I'll put numbers into the estimate sheet and return to you for sign-off before we send to Horizon. Want me to favor hitting their $10/1M target in the proposal?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation economics & throughput — post-demo next steps

Thanks — that framing is exactly what procurement and ops needed. A few quick notes: 

1) Procurement thinks Option A (6 x H100) is a good starting point if you can show the blended $/1M at about $10–$11. If Option A with the optimizations hits the $10 target, procurement can push forward in the $22k–$28k/mo range.
2) Ops confirms H100 preference; they also want the POC to validate the 08:00–11:00 window with our real traffic CSV (we'll share the CSV after internal approvals).
3) We'd like the contract sketch to include a 3-month trial/reservation with a 30-day exit clause tied to the POC acceptance criteria.

Next steps: please send Option A/B proposal and the POC runbook by EOD Wed 6/17 as discussed. We'll target to review and return comments by Fri 6/19.

Emily
